label: PF Backlog 574
title: Defect/RCCA: dev API is not session-scoped (fixed port 8000 + global URL) -> concurrent sessions 401/collide; unique port + discovery file + guard
body:
## Problem / why
The local dev PF API is NOT session-scoped: `scripts/dev/dev_server.py` binds a FIXED port (8000) and the worker
defaults to a GLOBAL URL (`pf_api_url = http://127.0.0.1:8000`). With >1 session on the same host (allowed by
IS-PF-0036 as long as they use separate folders), each folder generates its OWN `data/local/dev-api-token`
(different tokens), but they all target port 8000 -> only one server binds; a worker in session B hits session
A's server -> token mismatch -> 401. (Observed: `wg work` 401 'invalid or missing bearer token' after another
session's API was on 8000.)

## 5-Why (RCCA)
1. `wg work` got 401.
2. The worker sent its token to a server holding a different token.
3. Both session APIs target the same fixed port 8000; the worker URL is global, not session-scoped.
4. IS-PF-0036 isolates the working TREE but not the API endpoint (host+port) or its discovery.
ROOT CAUSE: the dev API endpoint (port + URL) is not session-scoped.

## Corrective
Make the dev API endpoint session-scoped: `dev_server.py` binds a free/unique port and writes a discovery file
`data/local/dev-api-url` next to `dev-api-token`; `workergrid/client._base()` falls back to it (like `token_file`).

## Guard
A check that the worker's resolved API URL+token belong to the same session/instance (or an explicit
`WORKERGRID_PF_API_URL`); and the dev launcher refuses to reuse a port owned by another PF instance.

## Acceptance (G/W/T)
- Given two sessions with separate folders, when both run `dev_server`, then each worker talks to ITS OWN API
  (no 401), using its own port + token.
- Given a foreign server on the worker's target port, then the worker fails closed with a clear message, not a silent 401.

## Related
IS-PF-0036 (one working tree per session); BI-PF-0457 (concurrent-session id clash - same class).
